stack: Backend: Java / Spring Boot 3.5.5, Spring Security (stateless JWT, HS256), Spring Data JPA, Flyway V1–V19, Razorpay SDK, Spring Mail
Frontend: React 19 + Vite 8 SPA (JavaScript), TanStack Query, axios
Database: PostgreSQL 16 (local docker-compose); a hosted Supabase Postgres is referenced in commented config
CI: 3 GitHub Actions workflows (branch auto-PR / merge only)
hosting: Frontend: Vercel (inferred from frontend-v1/vercel.json; not confirmed)
Backend: not defined in the repo (Dockerfile only; no deploy config)
Database: production provider not defined in the repo

scoring.formula: (Implemented × 1 + Partial × 0.5) ÷ applicable topics (all except Not Applicable Now)

topics.name: Rate Limiting
topics.verdict: Per-account login lockout and per-account email caps exist; no per-IP or API-wide limiting.
topics.applReason: Public signup/login/forgot-password endpoints are internet-facing.
topics.gap: No IP-keyed limiter, nothing on /auth/signup, nothing on /api/**; the lockout itself lets an attacker lock out a known user for 15 minutes.
topics.riskWhat: One IP can try passwords across thousands of emails, flood /auth/signup, and scrape or hammer any authenticated endpoint without limit.

plan.approach: Bucket4j servlet filter (com.bucket4j:bucket4j_jdk17-core) with in-memory buckets keyed by client IP for /auth/** and by user id for /api/**. Trust X-Forwarded-For only via server.forward-headers-strategy once a proxy is in place (PR-004).
tasks: Add bucket4j dependency to backend-v1/pom.xml.

Create common/security/RateLimitFilter.java: 10 req/min per IP on POST /auth/login, /auth/signup, /auth/forgot-password, /auth/resend-verification; 300 req/min per user on /api/**; respond 429 with Retry-After and errorCode RATE_LIMITED.
Register the filter before UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter in common/security/Security.java.
Expose limits as properties (app.rate-limit.*) in application.properties and backend-v1/.env.example.
Add RateLimitFilterTest (MockMvc) asserting the 11th login call in a minute returns 429.
acceptance: 11th POST /auth/login from one IP within 60 s returns 429 with a Retry-After header.
Normal usage (a user clicking through the app) never hits 429.
Limits are configurable via env without a rebuild.
plan.smoke: for i in $(seq 1 12); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"x@y.z","password":"bad"}'; done   # last lines must be 429
plan.cheaper: Cloudflare (free plan) rate-limiting rule on /auth/* at the edge — no code change, but needs PR-004/PR-097 to route traffic through Cloudflare.

topics.name: Caching
topics.verdict: Client-side query cache exists; no server cache is needed at current scale.
topics.applReason: Summaries are already single aggregate queries; data is tenant-scoped and changes often.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing breaks today; at high tenant counts dashboard queries repeat per page load.
topics.trigger: Dashboard/summary p95 > 300 ms or DB CPU > 60 % sustained → add Spring Cache (Caffeine) on plan/plan-feature lookups and summary queries with short TTLs.

topics.name: Load Balancing
topics.verdict: Single backend instance; no load balancer in the repo.
topics.applReason: One instance meets the SRS 99.5 % target with auto-restart.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing today.
topics.trigger: Running a second backend instance (also requires PR-038 ShedLock for the scheduler).

topics.name: Reverse Proxies
topics.verdict: No reverse proxy, ingress or PaaS router config in the repo; the backend serves plain HTTP on :8080.
topics.applReason: TLS termination, compression and real client IPs need a proxy or PaaS router in front of Spring Boot.
topics.gap: Hosting target for the backend is not defined anywhere in the repo (frontend has vercel.json; DB was previously Supabase per commented config).
topics.riskWhat: Without a proxy the API is either exposed over plain HTTP or not reachable; client IPs recorded in login_attempts and used for rate limiting are wrong.

plan.approach: Decide hosting first. Single VPS: Caddy 2 container in front of the backend (automatic Let's Encrypt TLS). PaaS (Render/Railway/Fly/Cloud Run): use the platform router and document it. Either way set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework.
tasks: Decide backend hosting (VPS + Docker Compose vs PaaS) and record it in docs/deployment.md.
VPS path: add a caddy service and Caddyfile (reverse_proxy backend:8080, encode gzip, HSTS header) to a production compose file.
Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework in application.properties so X-Forwarded-For/Proto are honoured.
Verify the backend container port is not published publicly (only Caddy on 80/443).
acceptance: https://api.<domain>/actuator/health returns 200 over HTTPS; http:// redirects to https://.
login_attempts.ip_address records the real client IP, not the proxy IP.
Port 8080 is not reachable from the internet.
plan.smoke: curl -sI https://api.<domain>/actuator/health | head -1; curl -sI http://api.<domain> | grep -i location
plan.cheaper: Put the PaaS default HTTPS URL behind Cloudflare proxy — no proxy container to maintain.

topics.name: API Gateways
topics.verdict: Single backend; auth and routing are handled inside Spring Security.
topics.applReason: One service, one API surface.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: A second service (e.g. the Python AI service in SRS §8) or public partner APIs needing keys/quotas.

topics.name: CDN
topics.verdict: vercel.json suggests the SPA is hosted on Vercel (which includes a CDN), but no deployment evidence is in the repo.
topics.applReason: Static SPA assets should be served from a CDN.
topics.riskWhat: If not on Vercel, assets are served from a single origin (slower, no edge caching).

plan.approach: Confirm the frontend is deployed on Vercel (or Cloudflare Pages/Netlify); record the project and domain.
tasks: Confirm the production frontend host and URL; add it to docs/deployment.md.
Check response headers of a hashed asset for a CDN cache hit (x-vercel-cache: HIT).
acceptance: A hashed JS asset returns a CDN cache-hit header.
plan.cheaper: Cloudflare Pages free tier.

topics.name: Edge Caching
topics.verdict: Depends on the frontend host's defaults; the API is authenticated and should not be edge-cached.
topics.applReason: Static assets only.
topics.riskWhat: Slower first loads if assets are not cached at the edge.

plan.approach: Add explicit Cache-Control headers in vercel.json: immutable for /assets/*, no-cache for index.html.
tasks: Add a headers block to frontend-v1/vercel.json: /assets/(.*) → 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'; /index.html → 'no-cache'.
acceptance: Hashed assets return max-age=31536000, immutable; index.html returns no-cache.
plan.cheaper: Rely on Vercel defaults (already sensible).

topics.name: Cache Invalidation
topics.verdict: No server caches exist; Vite emits content-hashed asset names so a deploy invalidates assets automatically.
topics.applReason: Nothing cached server-side.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: When PR-002 server caching is added: evict on write (@CacheEvict) for the cached entity.

topics.name: WAF
topics.verdict: No WAF or managed rule set in front of the app.
topics.applReason: Public SaaS with login, signup and payment endpoints.
topics.riskWhat: Common exploit probes and bot traffic reach the app directly.

plan.approach: Cloudflare proxy (orange-cloud) in front of api.<domain> with the free managed WAF ruleset; Vercel Firewall for the frontend.
tasks: Move DNS for the domain to Cloudflare (PR-097).
Proxy api.<domain> through Cloudflare; enable Free Managed Ruleset and Bot Fight Mode.
Restrict origin to Cloudflare IP ranges (firewall on the VPS or PaaS allowlist).
acceptance: A request with a basic SQLi probe in the query string is blocked at the edge (403 from Cloudflare).
Origin is not reachable bypassing Cloudflare.
plan.cheaper: Skip WAF initially; rely on rate limiting (PR-001) and input validation — acceptable for a closed beta.

topics.name: DDoS Protection
topics.verdict: No DDoS protection configured for the backend origin.
topics.applReason: Internet-facing API.
topics.riskWhat: A volumetric or L7 flood takes the single instance down.

plan.approach: Same Cloudflare proxy as PR-074 (unmetered DDoS mitigation on all plans).
tasks: Proxy api.<domain> through Cloudflare.
Enable 'Under Attack' runbook step in docs/runbooks/backend-down.md.
acceptance: DNS for api.<domain> resolves to Cloudflare IPs.
plan.cheaper: Platform-level protection of the chosen PaaS if it offers it.

topics.name: DNS
topics.verdict: No domain, DNS records or DNS-as-code in the repo; FRONTEND_URL defaults to localhost.
topics.applReason: Users need stable HTTPS hostnames; email links use FRONTEND_URL.
topics.riskWhat: Email verification/reset links point to the wrong host if FRONTEND_URL is not set.

plan.approach: Register/confirm the domain in Cloudflare DNS; app.<domain> → frontend host, api.<domain> → backend.
tasks: Create DNS records for app.<domain> and api.<domain>.
Set FRONTEND_URL and VITE_API_URL to the production hostnames.
Document records in docs/deployment.md.
acceptance: Verification email link opens https://app.<domain>/verify-email?token=…
plan.cheaper: Use the hosts' default subdomains (*.vercel.app, *.onrender.com) for a pilot.

topics.name: CI/CD
topics.verdict: Workflows only open PRs and merge branches; nothing builds, tests or deploys.
evidence: .github/workflows/01 dev branch to development.yml:11-14, 62 (opens a PR only)
.github/workflows/02 deploy development to testing.yml:17-18, 60-61 (git merge + push, no build)
topics.applReason: Any change can reach development/testing without compiling.
topics.gap: No CI job runs mvn test or npm build/lint; no deploy job; no required status checks.
topics.riskWhat: Broken builds and failing tests merge unnoticed; auto-merge.yml pushes every dev-* branch straight into development.

plan.approach: GitHub Actions ci.yml with two jobs plus branch protection on development/testing/main.
tasks: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: job backend (actions/setup-java@v4 temurin 25, cache maven, ./mvnw -B verify in backend-v1); job frontend (actions/setup-node@v4 cache npm, npm ci, npm run lint, npm run build in frontend-v1).
Trigger on pull_request to development, testing, main and on push to those branches.
Add branch protection: require both checks before merge on development/testing/main.
Change auto-merge.yml to open a PR (like workflow 01) instead of pushing directly, or delete it.
Add a deploy job (after PR-007) that builds and pushes the image tagged with the git SHA to GHCR on push to main.
acceptance: A PR with a failing backend test shows a red 'backend' check and cannot be merged.
CI finishes in < 15 min with caches warm.
Nothing reaches development without passing CI.
plan.smoke: gh workflow run ci.yml --ref development && gh run watch
plan.cheaper: Only add the two CI jobs and branch protection now; postpone the deploy job.

topics.name: Docker
topics.verdict: A backend Dockerfile exists but builds inside a JDK image as root, skips tests and has no .dockerignore.
evidence: backend-v1/.env (exists locally, gitignored but not dockerignored)
topics.applReason: The image is the deployable unit.
topics.gap: Single stage on eclipse-temurin:25-jdk, COPY . ., -DskipTests, root user, no HEALTHCHECK, no JVM memory flags, shell-form CMD with a glob.
topics.riskWhat: COPY . . with no .dockerignore copies backend-v1/.env (present locally) into the image layers, leaking secrets; large root-run image; no healthcheck.

plan.approach: Multi-stage Dockerfile: maven build stage → eclipse-temurin:25-jre runtime, non-root user, .dockerignore.
tasks: Add backend-v1/.dockerignore excluding .env*, target/, .git, *.md, .idea, .vscode.
Stage 1 (eclipse-temurin:25-jdk): copy mvnw, .mvn, pom.xml; ./mvnw -B dependency:go-offline; copy src; ./mvnw -B package (tests run in CI, so -DskipTests is acceptable here only if CI is required).
Stage 2 (eclipse-temurin:25-jre): copy the jar as app.jar, create user 'app', USER app, ENTRYPOINT ["java","-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75","-jar","/app/app.jar"].
Add HEALTHCHECK using curl/wget on /actuator/health (after PR-056).
Verify no .env inside the image: docker run --rm --entrypoint ls <image> -la /app.
acceptance: Image runs as non-root (docker run --rm id shows uid ≠ 0).
No .env file exists in any image layer.
Image size < 350 MB.
plan.smoke: docker build -t crm-backend ./backend-v1 && docker run --rm --entrypoint sh crm-backend -c 'id; ls -la /app'
plan.cheaper: Keep the single stage but add .dockerignore and USER — removes the secret leak with 10 minutes of work.

topics.name: Kubernetes
topics.verdict: No Kubernetes manifests; one backend service does not need an orchestrator.
topics.applReason: Compose or a PaaS covers one service + Postgres.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: More than ~3 services, autoscaling needs, or an enterprise customer requiring a k8s deployment.

topics.name: Feature Flags
topics.verdict: One env-driven boolean flag exists (sales-team scope); no runtime or per-tenant toggles.
topics.applReason: Static flags are enough for the current release cadence.
topics.gap: No mechanism to switch features per tenant or at runtime (needed for AI rollout per the AI split report).
topics.riskWhat: Turning a feature off needs a redeploy.

plan.approach: Keep @Value flags; when AI ships add a feature_flags table (tenant_id nullable, key, enabled) read through a FeatureFlags service with a 60 s cache.
tasks: Create Flyway migration feature_flags(tenant_id, key, enabled).
Add common/flags/FeatureFlags.java with isEnabled(key, tenantId).
Expose a super-admin toggle endpoint.
acceptance: Toggling a flag for one tenant changes behaviour within 60 s without a deploy.
plan.cheaper: Unleash/FF4j are heavier; env flags are fine until AI rollout.

topics.name: Blue-Green Deployment
topics.verdict: Single instance; brief restart downtime is acceptable at the SRS 99.5 % target.
topics.riskWhat: A deploy causes a few seconds of 502s.
topics.trigger: Enterprise SLA above 99.9 % or deploys during business hours causing user-visible errors.

topics.name: Canary Releases
topics.verdict: Not needed with a single instance and a small user base.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Multiple instances and enough traffic for a 5 % canary to be meaningful.

topics.name: Rolling Deployments
topics.verdict: Single instance; Spring Boot 3.5 shuts down gracefully by default, which is enough for now.
topics.riskWhat: Short downtime per deploy.
topics.trigger: Second instance behind a load balancer (PR-003).

topics.name: Rollbacks
topics.verdict: No versioned artifacts or rollback procedure; DB rollback scripts exist only for V16–V19.
topics.applReason: A bad deploy must be reversible in minutes.
topics.gap: Images are not tagged/pushed anywhere; no documented 'deploy previous version' step; migrations V1–V15 have no down scripts and no expand/contract rule.
topics.riskWhat: A broken release can only be fixed forward by rebuilding from source.

plan.approach: Immutable images tagged with the git SHA in GHCR; rollback = redeploy the previous tag. Migrations follow expand/contract so the previous app version still runs on the new schema.
tasks: In ci.yml deploy job push ghcr.io/<org>/crm-backend:<sha> and :latest.
Write docs/runbooks/rollback.md: identify previous SHA, redeploy it, when to run db/rollback scripts.
Add a PR template checkbox: 'migration is backward compatible (expand/contract)'.
acceptance: Rolling back to the previous SHA takes < 10 minutes following the runbook in a staging drill.
plan.smoke: docker pull ghcr.io/<org>/crm-backend:<previous-sha> && docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
plan.cheaper: Keep the last two built jars on the server and switch a symlink.

topics.name: Infrastructure as Code
topics.verdict: No IaC or production deployment definition; only a local Postgres compose file.
topics.applReason: The production setup must be reproducible by someone other than its creator.
topics.riskWhat: Rebuilding the environment after loss depends on memory.

plan.approach: For a VPS: deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml + Caddyfile + .env.example is the IaC. For a PaaS: commit its blueprint file (render.yaml / fly.toml).
tasks: Create deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml (backend image by tag, caddy, optional postgres if self-hosted).
Commit the platform blueprint if a PaaS is chosen.
Document bootstrap in docs/deployment.md.
acceptance: A new environment comes up from the repo + secrets only, following docs/deployment.md.
plan.cheaper: Written runbook only.

topics.name: Terraform
topics.verdict: Not needed until cloud resources outgrow a compose file or PaaS blueprint.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Managing several cloud resources (VPC, managed DB, buckets, DNS) across environments.

topics.name: Helm Charts
topics.verdict: No Kubernetes, so no Helm.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Adopting Kubernetes (PR-008).

topics.name: Build Caching
topics.verdict: Docker build re-downloads all Maven dependencies on every change; no CI caches.
topics.applReason: Slow builds slow every deploy and PR.
topics.riskWhat: Long build times; flaky builds when Maven Central is slow.

plan.approach: Dependency layer in Docker and setup-* caches in CI.
tasks: Dockerfile: copy pom.xml/mvnw/.mvn first and run ./mvnw dependency:go-offline before copying src (part of PR-007).
ci.yml: setup-java with cache: maven; setup-node with cache: npm.
Optional: docker/build-push-action with cache-to/cache-from type=gha.
acceptance: Second CI run with no dependency change is ≥ 40 % faster.
plan.cheaper: Only the Dockerfile layer change.

topics.name: Dependency Hell
topics.verdict: Lockfile and pinned Maven versions exist; no vulnerability scanning or update automation; Java version is inconsistent.
evidence: backend-v1/pom.xml:10-11, 62-63, 75-87, 141-142 (pinned versions under Spring Boot BOM)
topics.applReason: Known CVEs in dependencies ship silently.
topics.gap: No Dependabot/Renovate, no npm audit or OWASP dependency-check in CI; pom targets Java 17 while the build image and local builds use JDK 25.
topics.riskWhat: Vulnerable transitive dependencies; builds differ between JDK 17 and 25.

plan.approach: Dependabot for maven, npm and github-actions; audits in CI; pin the JDK.
tasks: Add .github/dependabot.yml (weekly; ecosystems maven /backend-v1, npm /frontend-v1, github-actions /).
In ci.yml add 'npm audit --audit-level=high' and 'mvn -B org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check -DfailBuildOnCVSS=8'.
Set java.version and the Docker/CI JDK to the same release (decide 17 LTS vs 25) and document it in backend-v1/README.md.
acceptance: Dependabot opens update PRs weekly.
CI fails on a high-severity npm advisory.
plan.cheaper: GitHub's free Dependabot alerts only (no CI gate).

topics.name: Service Discovery
topics.verdict: Monolith with fixed hostnames; nothing to discover.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Multiple internal services (e.g. AI service) with dynamic instances.

topics.name: Circuit Breakers
topics.verdict: Only two outbound dependencies (Razorpay at checkout, SMTP after commit); a breaker adds little today.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing today.
topics.trigger: Module 5 integrations (WhatsApp/SMS/email API) or the AI provider go live → Resilience4j circuit breakers around each client.

topics.name: Timeouts
topics.verdict: The frontend has a 30 s HTTP timeout; no server-side timeouts are configured for SMTP, Razorpay, JDBC or transactions.
evidence: backend-v1/src/main/java/com/company/crm/auth/service/AuthService.java:186-191 (mail sent in afterCommit on the request thread)
topics.applReason: Emails are sent on the request thread after commit; JavaMail's default is an infinite timeout.
topics.riskWhat: A hung SMTP server blocks signup/forgot-password request threads indefinitely until Tomcat's pool (200) is exhausted and the API stops responding.

plan.approach: Explicit timeouts on every outbound call and on transactions.
tasks: Add spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.connectiontimeout=5000, timeout=5000, writetimeout=5000 to application.properties.
Add spring.transaction.default-timeout=30 and spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=5000.

Razorpay: check whether razorpay-java 1.4.8 accepts a custom OkHttp client/timeouts; if not, call createOrder via CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(...).orTimeout(10, SECONDS) and map timeouts to 502 PAYMENT_GATEWAY_ERROR.
Add a test with a fake SMTP server that never answers (GreenMail with delay) asserting the request returns within 7 s.
acceptance: With SMTP blackholed, POST /auth/forgot-password returns within 7 s.
Razorpay outage makes checkout fail within 10 s with a clear error.
plan.smoke: iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 587 -j DROP; time curl -X POST $API/auth/forgot-password -d '{"email":"a@b.c"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
plan.cheaper: Only the three mail timeout properties — covers the most dangerous case.

topics.name: Retries
topics.verdict: The frontend retries failed queries; server-side email sends are not retried — failures are logged and dropped.
topics.applReason: Verification and password-reset emails are the only way into the product.
topics.riskWhat: A transient SMTP error leaves a user without a verification or reset link.

plan.approach: Spring Retry on MailService sends now; DB outbox when Module 5 arrives.
tasks: Add spring-retry + spring-boot-starter-aop; @EnableRetry.
Annotate the internal send method with @Retryable(retryFor = MailException.class, maxAttempts = 3, backoff = @Backoff(delay = 2000, multiplier = 2)).
Keep the final failure log at ERROR with the recipient domain only (no token).
acceptance: A send that fails twice then succeeds delivers one email.
Three failures produce exactly one ERROR log.
plan.smoke: Unit test with a mocked JavaMailSender throwing twice.
plan.cheaper: Let users trigger 'Resend' (already available) and accept occasional loss.

topics.name: Exponential Backoff
topics.verdict: TanStack Query uses exponential backoff for query retries; server retries do not exist yet.
topics.applReason: Pairs with PR-012.
topics.riskWhat: Retry storms if retries are added without backoff.

plan.approach: Use @Backoff(multiplier=2) in PR-012; same rule for future integration clients.
tasks: Covered by the PR-012 @Retryable backoff settings.
acceptance: Retry delays observed in logs are 2 s then 4 s.

topics.name: Idempotency
topics.verdict: Payments and ticket claims are idempotent; create endpoints and lead conversion are not.
topics.applReason: Double submits and retries create duplicate customers/leads/quotations.
topics.gap: No Idempotency-Key support on POST creates; LeadService.changeStage (lines 103-123) checks convertedCustomer == null without a row lock.
topics.riskWhat: A double-clicked or retried create makes duplicate records; a double 'Converted' request can create two customers.

plan.approach: Idempotency-Key header for POST creates + a row lock on lead conversion.
tasks: Create idempotency_keys table (tenant_id, key, request_hash, response_json, created_at) via Flyway.
Add common/web/IdempotencyFilter.java: for POST with Idempotency-Key, return the stored response on repeat within 24 h.
Send a UUID Idempotency-Key from the frontend api.service apipost for create calls.
Add LeadRepository.findForUpdate (PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) and use it in changeStage.
acceptance: Two identical POST /api/customers with the same Idempotency-Key create one customer.
Two concurrent 'converted' stage changes create one customer.
plan.smoke: K=$(uuidgen); for i in 1 2; do curl -s -X POST $API/api/customers -H "Idempotency-Key: $K" -H 'Authorization: Bearer '$T -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @cust.json; done
plan.cheaper: Only the lead-conversion row lock (smallest real data-integrity risk).

topics.name: Backpressure
topics.verdict: Ticket lists are paged with a size cap; every other list endpoint loads all tenant rows into memory.
topics.applReason: Large tenants will make list endpoints slow and memory-heavy.
topics.riskWhat: A tenant with 100k leads makes GET /api/leads load all rows into the heap on each call.

plan.approach: Extend opt-in paging to all list endpoints and push filters into SQL.
tasks: Add page/size/sort params via PageRequestFactory to customers, leads, opportunities, quotations, campaigns controllers.
Replace in-memory filters with Specification/JPQL predicates.
Switch frontend list pages to paged requests.
acceptance: GET /api/leads?page=0&size=50 returns ≤ 50 rows with totalElements.
Heap stays flat when listing a 100k-lead tenant.
plan.cheaper: Hard cap of 1000 rows per list response as a stopgap.

topics.name: Health Checks
topics.verdict: No health endpoint at all; the backend README points to /api/test, which does not exist.
topics.applReason: Any host, load balancer or uptime monitor needs one.
topics.riskWhat: The platform cannot detect a dead or DB-disconnected backend; outages go unnoticed.

plan.approach: Spring Boot Actuator health endpoint, public but minimal.
tasks: Add spring-boot-starter-actuator to backend-v1/pom.xml.
application.properties: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info,prometheus; management.endpoint.health.show-details=never.
Permit GET /actuator/health and /actuator/info in Security.java; keep others authenticated or on a separate management port.
Fix backend-v1/README.md to reference /actuator/health.
acceptance: GET /actuator/health returns {"status":"UP"} without auth.
Stopping Postgres turns it DOWN (503).

topics.name: Liveness and Readiness Probes
topics.verdict: No liveness/readiness distinction (no health endpoint).
topics.applReason: Hosts should not route traffic until Flyway and the DB pool are ready.
topics.riskWhat: Traffic hits the app during startup/migrations and gets errors.

plan.approach: Actuator probe groups.
tasks: Set management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true; readiness group includes db.
Point the host's health check to /actuator/health/readiness and the Docker HEALTHCHECK to /actuator/health/liveness.
acceptance: /actuator/health/readiness is DOWN until migrations finish and UP afterwards.
plan.cheaper: Single /actuator/health check.

topics.name: Failover
topics.verdict: Single instance; auto-restart by the host is enough for 99.5 % (≈ 3.6 h/month).
topics.riskWhat: An instance crash means downtime until restart.
topics.trigger: Enterprise SLA ≥ 99.9 % → second instance + managed DB with automatic failover.

topics.name: Multi-Region Deployment
topics.verdict: Not needed for an India-first SaaS with modest load.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Customers in other continents with latency or data-residency requirements.

topics.name: Chaos Engineering
topics.verdict: Premature before monitoring, alerts and runbooks exist.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: After SLOs and alerting are live for a quarter; start with manual game days.

topics.name: Message Queues
topics.verdict: No asynchronous workloads beyond transactional email.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing today.
topics.trigger: Module 5 (WhatsApp/SMS/email campaigns) or AI jobs → start with a Postgres outbox table + worker before adding RabbitMQ/SQS.

topics.name: Pub/Sub
topics.verdict: Single consumer per event; no fan-out need.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Several modules reacting to the same domain event across processes.

topics.name: Event-Driven Architecture
topics.verdict: Post-commit email hooks exist; a broader event model is not needed yet.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Notifications/escalations (SRS §17) → Spring ApplicationEvents with @TransactionalEventListener.

topics.name: Distributed Transactions
topics.verdict: One database; the payment flow is handled by idempotent verify + webhook instead.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: A second datastore (e.g. MongoDB per SRS) written in the same business operation.

topics.name: Saga Pattern
topics.verdict: No multi-service workflows.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Multi-step flows spanning services/providers (e.g. ERP order sync).

topics.name: Dead Letter Queues
topics.verdict: No queue exists; failed emails are a retry problem (PR-012).
topics.riskWhat: Nothing beyond PR-012.
topics.trigger: Introducing PR-015 queues/outbox → failed rows after N attempts move to a dead-letter status/table with an admin view.

topics.name: Cron Jobs
topics.verdict: One scheduled job refreshes subscription statuses; no lock, no explicit time zone, no run monitoring.
topics.applReason: Subscription expiry drives read-only mode for tenants.
topics.riskWhat: With two instances the job runs twice; a silently failing job leaves expired tenants active (or vice versa).

plan.approach: ShedLock + explicit zone + a run metric.
tasks: Add net.javacrumbs.shedlock:shedlock-spring and shedlock-provider-jdbc-template; Flyway table shedlock.
Annotate refreshStatuses with @SchedulerLock(name = "subscriptionExpiry", lockAtMostFor = "10m").
Set @Scheduled(zone = "Asia/Kolkata") or app.timezone property.
Increment a Micrometer counter per run and alert if no run in 2 h (after PR-061).
acceptance: With two instances running, the job executes once per schedule (one shedlock row update).
plan.smoke: SELECT name, lock_until, locked_by FROM shedlock;
plan.cheaper: Run a single instance only (documented constraint).

topics.name: WebSockets
topics.verdict: No realtime features today.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Live pipeline updates (SRS AC-3.1b) or chat.

topics.name: Long Polling
topics.verdict: Not used and not needed.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.

topics.name: Server-Sent Events
topics.verdict: Not used yet.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: In-app notifications (SRS §17) → SSE endpoint for the navbar bell is the simplest fit.

topics.name: TCP vs UDP
topics.verdict: All traffic is HTTP over TCP; nothing needs UDP.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.

topics.name: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3
topics.verdict: Negotiated by the edge/proxy (not in repo); Tomcat runs HTTP/1.1 (server.http2.enabled not set).
topics.applReason: Handled at the edge.
topics.riskWhat: Slightly slower asset loading if the edge only speaks HTTP/1.1.

plan.approach: Confirm the edge (Vercel/Cloudflare/Caddy) negotiates h2/h3; no app change needed.
tasks: Check with curl --http2.
acceptance: curl reports HTTP/2 for app and api hosts.

topics.name: gRPC
topics.verdict: No internal service-to-service calls.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.

topics.name: Webhooks
topics.verdict: Razorpay webhook is signature-verified and processed idempotently under a row lock.
topics.applReason: Payment confirmation must not depend on the browser.
topics.gap: Minor: no stored log of received webhook events for audit/replay.

topics.name: Database Indexing
topics.verdict: Tenant/owner indexes on every table plus composite dashboard indexes, verified by a test.

topics.name: Query Optimization
topics.verdict: Dashboard summaries are single SQL aggregates; list endpoints filter in Java and quotation numbers use COUNT(*).
topics.riskWhat: List latency grows linearly with tenant size; the SRS 2 s search target will be missed for large tenants.

plan.approach: Push filters/search into SQL and page results (with PR-044); enable slow-query visibility.
tasks: Rewrite list filters as JPA Specifications or @Query with optional params.
Add pg_trgm GIN index for name search if ILIKE is used.
Enable pg_stat_statements on the production DB and review top queries monthly.
acceptance: GET /api/leads?search=abc on 100k leads returns in < 300 ms.
plan.smoke: EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the generated query shows an index scan.
plan.cheaper: Add LIMIT + DB-side search only for leads and customers.

topics.name: N+1 Queries
topics.verdict: Tickets, subscriptions and teams use @EntityGraph; leads, customers, opportunities, quotations and campaigns load associations per row.
topics.applReason: Every list page runs 1 + N×(associations) queries.
topics.riskWhat: Lists of a few hundred records issue hundreds of queries; latency and DB load spike.

plan.approach: Global batch fetching now, entity graphs on hot list queries next.
tasks: Set spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=50 in application.properties.
Add @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"owner","campaign","convertedCustomer"}) to LeadRepository.findByTenantId* (same for customer/opportunity/quotation).
Add a test with hibernate.generate_statistics asserting statement count for a 100-row list.
acceptance: Listing 100 leads executes ≤ 5 SQL statements.
plan.smoke: Run with SHOW_SQL=true and count 'select' lines for GET /api/leads
plan.cheaper: Only default_batch_fetch_size (one line).

topics.name: Connection Pooling
topics.verdict: HikariCP is active by Spring Boot default but untuned (pool size 10, no leak detection, no max-lifetime vs DB pooler).
topics.applReason: Pool size must match the DB/pooler connection limit.
topics.riskWhat: Pool exhaustion or 'connection closed' errors behind a pooler like Supabase's.

plan.approach: Explicit Hikari settings.
tasks: Set spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size (≤ DB limit / instances), minimum-idle=2, connection-timeout=5000, max-lifetime below the DB/pooler idle timeout, leak-detection-threshold=20000.
acceptance: Under 50 concurrent requests no 'Connection is not available' errors; no leak warnings.
plan.cheaper: Keep defaults but set max-lifetime when using a pooler.

topics.name: Read Replicas
topics.verdict: Read load is small; one primary suffices.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Primary CPU > 70 % from reporting queries → route reports to a replica.

topics.name: Sharding
topics.verdict: Tenant-scoped single database is right for this size.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Tens of thousands of tenants or a single DB > ~1 TB.

topics.name: Partitioning
topics.verdict: No table is large yet; login_attempts and audit_events will grow without retention.
topics.riskWhat: Unbounded growth of login_attempts/audit_events over years.
topics.trigger: login_attempts/audit_events > ~10M rows → monthly range partitions; add a retention job (e.g. delete login_attempts > 90 days) sooner.

topics.name: Replication
topics.verdict: Production database HA/replication is a hosting concern not visible in the repo.
topics.applReason: Data durability for paying tenants.
topics.riskWhat: A single unreplicated DB disk failure loses data back to the last backup.

plan.approach: Use a managed Postgres (Supabase/Neon/RDS) with HA, or document why not.
tasks: Confirm the production DB provider and plan; record HA/replication status in docs/deployment.md.
acceptance: Provider dashboard shows HA/standby or the risk is accepted in writing.
plan.cheaper: Managed DB without HA + tested backups (PR-084).

topics.name: Database Migrations
topics.verdict: Flyway runs V1–V19 on startup with Hibernate in validate mode; a migration test exists.
topics.gap: V2__add_ai_modules.sql is an empty placeholder; rollback scripts exist only for V16–V19.

topics.name: Schema Versioning
topics.verdict: Sequential Flyway versions with flyway_schema_history; ddl-auto=validate catches drift at startup.

topics.name: Leader Election
topics.verdict: Single instance; only one scheduled job.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing today.
topics.trigger: Second instance → ShedLock (PR-021/PR-038) is sufficient; no full leader election needed.

topics.name: CAP Theorem
topics.verdict: One PostgreSQL primary — strongly consistent by design.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Multi-region or multi-datastore writes.

topics.name: Eventual Consistency
topics.verdict: All reads hit the primary; no async projections.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Read replicas or caches (PR-029/PR-002).

topics.name: Optimistic Locking
topics.verdict: No @Version on any entity; concurrent edits silently overwrite each other.
topics.applReason: Several roles edit the same customers, leads, quotations and tickets.
topics.riskWhat: Two users editing a quotation or ticket: the later save erases the earlier one with no warning.

plan.approach: JPA @Version on mutable aggregates; 409 on conflict.
tasks: Flyway V2x: add version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 to customers, leads, opportunities, quotations, service_tickets, campaigns.
Add @Version private Long version to those entities and include version in their Req/Res DTOs.
Map ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException to 409 CONFLICT in GlobalExceptionHandler (frontend already shows the 409 message in core/utils/apiError.js).
acceptance: Saving a quotation with a stale version returns 409 'Someone else changed this'.
plan.smoke: Two PUTs with the same version → second gets 409
plan.cheaper: Only quotations and tickets (highest contention).

topics.name: Pessimistic Locking
topics.verdict: Used where it matters: payment confirmation row lock and an atomic conditional update for ticket claims.

topics.name: Distributed Locks
topics.verdict: Single instance.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing today.
topics.trigger: Second instance → ShedLock JDBC for scheduled jobs (see PR-021).

topics.name: Race Conditions
topics.verdict: Payments and ticket claims are race-safe; quotation numbering and lead conversion are not.
topics.applReason: Both happen in normal use.
topics.riskWhat: Two quotations created at once in a tenant get the same QTN number → unique violation → 500; a double 'converted' request can create two customers.

plan.approach: Per-tenant sequence with a row lock; lock the lead on conversion.
tasks: Flyway: tenant_counters(tenant_id, name, next_value); QuotationService takes the next value with SELECT … FOR UPDATE.
Use LeadRepository.findForUpdate in changeStage (shared with PR-014).
acceptance: 50 parallel quotation creates in one tenant all succeed with distinct numbers.
plan.smoke: seq 50 | xargs -P 50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $API/api/quotations … | sort | uniq -c
plan.cheaper: Catch DataIntegrityViolationException and retry the insert once.

topics.name: Deadlocks
topics.verdict: Very few explicit locks (one payment row per transaction); deadlock risk is negligible today.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing observed.
topics.trigger: Adding multi-row locking (counters, batch jobs) → lock rows in a consistent order; monitor pg_stat_database.deadlocks.

topics.name: Memory Leaks
topics.verdict: Requires runtime heap metrics; none are collected.
topics.riskWhat: Unbounded list loading (PR-044) can look like a leak under load.

plan.approach: JVM memory metrics via Actuator/Micrometer; heap dump on OOM.
tasks: After PR-061, chart jvm_memory_used_bytes per area.
Add -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/tmp to the container ENTRYPOINT.
acceptance: Heap after GC stays flat over a 1-hour soak test.
plan.cheaper: Watch container memory in the host dashboard.

topics.name: Garbage Collection
topics.verdict: JDK defaults (G1, container-aware) apply; no heap sizing is set for the container.
topics.riskWhat: Default MaxRAMPercentage=25 wastes 75 % of container memory or causes early OOM on small instances.

plan.approach: Set heap relative to container memory.
tasks: Use -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 in ENTRYPOINT (part of PR-007).
acceptance: java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version inside the container shows MaxHeapSize ≈ 75 % of the limit.
plan.smoke: docker run --rm -m 1g crm-backend java -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version | grep MaxHeapSize

topics.name: Thread Safety
topics.verdict: Services are stateless singletons with final injected dependencies; per-request state lives in the SecurityContext.

topics.name: Network Partitions
topics.verdict: Single app + single DB; a partition is simply an outage.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing beyond PR-056.
topics.trigger: Multi-instance or multi-region.

topics.name: Clock Skew
topics.verdict: Single server issues and validates JWTs (no skew issue), but all dates use the JVM default zone, so behaviour depends on the host time zone.
topics.applReason: Users are in India; containers usually run in UTC.
topics.riskWhat: 'Today', SLA due times, reporting periods and the subscription cron shift by 5.5 h on a UTC host.

plan.approach: Pin the application time zone.
tasks: Add -Duser.timezone=Asia/Kolkata (or TZ env) to the container, or add app.timezone and use Clock.system(ZoneId.of(...)).
Set hibernate.jdbc.time_zone=UTC if storing UTC.
acceptance: On a UTC host, 'resolved this week' starts Monday 00:00 IST.
plan.smoke: docker run --rm -e TZ=UTC crm-backend … and compare ReportingPeriods output
plan.cheaper: Set TZ=Asia/Kolkata env on the host.

topics.name: Autoscaling
topics.verdict: Load does not justify it; horizontal scaling isn't fully safe yet (PR-046).
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Sustained CPU > 70 % on the largest sensible instance.

topics.name: Horizontal Scaling
topics.verdict: Stateless JWT and DB-held state allow multiple instances, but the scheduled job has no lock.
topics.riskWhat: Running two instances duplicates the subscription job.

plan.approach: Make it safe before needing it.
tasks: Implement PR-021 ShedLock.
Verify no in-memory state (rate-limit buckets from PR-001 become per-instance — move to Bucket4j JDBC/Redis backend if scaling).
acceptance: Two instances behind a proxy pass the full test suite and run the job once.
plan.cheaper: Stay single-instance and scale vertically.

topics.name: Vertical Scaling
topics.verdict: Instance size is a hosting setting not visible in the repo; heap sizing missing (PR-042).

plan.approach: Document instance size and memory limit; size heap with PR-042.
tasks: Record CPU/RAM of the production instance in docs/deployment.md.
acceptance: Documented size matches the host.

topics.name: Cost Optimization
topics.verdict: Depends on the hosting decision (PR-004).
topics.riskWhat: Overpaying or under-provisioning.

plan.approach: Pick the cheapest host that meets 99.5 % with backups and TLS; review monthly.
tasks: Compare 2–3 options (single VPS + managed Postgres vs PaaS) and record the choice.
acceptance: Monthly cost recorded and reviewed.
plan.cheaper: Single small VPS + managed Postgres free/hobby tier for a pilot.

topics.name: Cold Starts
topics.verdict: If the backend lands on a scale-to-zero platform, JVM + Flyway + Hibernate startup will add seconds to the first request.
topics.applReason: Depends on hosting.
topics.riskWhat: First login after idle takes 10–30 s or times out.

plan.approach: Keep min instances ≥ 1; optionally use CDS/AOT to cut startup.
tasks: Set min instances = 1 on the chosen PaaS.
Optional: -XX:+AutoCreateSharedArchive -XX:SharedArchiveFile=/app/app.jsa.
acceptance: Startup < 15 s; no cold start after idle.
plan.smoke: time curl -fsS https://api.<domain>/actuator/health after 1 h idle
plan.cheaper: Always-on VPS (no cold starts).

topics.name: Serverless Limits
topics.verdict: Nothing runs serverless (frontend is static, backend is a container).
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Moving any part to Lambda/Cloud Functions.

topics.name: Latency
topics.verdict: No latency measurement exists; SRS sets 3 s dashboard / 2 s search targets.
topics.applReason: Targets can't be verified.
topics.riskWhat: Slow pages go unnoticed until users complain.

plan.approach: Micrometer http.server.requests timers + k6 smoke test.
tasks: After PR-061 enable percentiles histogram for http.server.requests.
Write load/smoke.js (k6) hitting login, dashboard summary, leads list.
acceptance: k6 report shows dashboard p95 < 3 s and search p95 < 2 s at 20 VUs.
plan.cheaper: Browser devtools timings on staging.

topics.name: Throughput
topics.verdict: No throughput baseline.
topics.riskWhat: Unknown capacity.

plan.approach: k6 ramp test to find max RPS per instance.
tasks: Add load/ramp.js ramping 10→200 VUs; record max RPS before p95 > 2 s.
acceptance: Capacity number recorded in docs/deployment.md.

topics.name: P99 Latency
topics.verdict: Requires histograms; none collected.
topics.riskWhat: Tail slowness invisible.

plan.approach: management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.http.server.requests=true; Grafana panel for p99.
tasks: Enable histogram property.
Add p99 panel.
acceptance: p99 visible per endpoint.

topics.name: Tail Latency
topics.verdict: No visibility into slow outliers.
topics.riskWhat: Occasional very slow requests unexplained.

plan.approach: Slow-request log + p99 alerts.
tasks: Log requests > 2 s with path and duration (filter).
Alert on p99 > 5 s (after PR-062).
acceptance: Requests > 2 s appear in logs with request-id.

topics.name: Monitoring
topics.verdict: No uptime monitor, APM or metrics endpoint.
topics.applReason: Nobody is told when production is down.
topics.riskWhat: Outages are discovered by customers.

plan.approach: External uptime check on /actuator/health + Actuator metrics scraped by Grafana Cloud (free tier).
tasks: Create Better Stack (or UptimeRobot) monitors for https://api.<domain>/actuator/health and https://app.<domain> every 1 min.
After PR-061, connect Grafana Cloud Prometheus scrape (or Grafana Agent) to /actuator/prometheus.
acceptance: Stopping the backend triggers a monitor DOWN within 2 minutes.
plan.smoke: docker stop crm-backend; wait 2 min; check monitor status
plan.cheaper: UptimeRobot free (5-min checks).

topics.name: Logging
topics.verdict: SLF4J/Logback to stdout with env-controlled levels; no structured logs, request IDs or central storage.
topics.riskWhat: Incidents can't be traced across requests; logs vanish with the container.

plan.approach: Spring Boot 3.5 structured JSON logs + MDC request id + log shipping.
tasks: Set logging.structured.format.console=ecs in production profile.
Add common/web/RequestIdFilter.java: read/generate X-Request-Id, put in MDC, return in response header (also closes API-4/ERR-2 from the SRS report).
Ship container stdout to Better Stack Logs or Grafana Loki; 30-day retention.
acceptance: Every log line is JSON with request_id; the same id is returned in the X-Request-Id response header.
plan.cheaper: Keep plain logs but add the request-id filter.

topics.name: Distributed Tracing
topics.verdict: Single service; request IDs (PR-059) are enough.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: A second service (AI FastAPI) → Micrometer Tracing + OpenTelemetry exporter.

topics.name: Metrics
topics.verdict: No Micrometer registry or metrics endpoint.
topics.riskWhat: No data for latency, errors, JVM or pool health.

plan.approach: micrometer-registry-prometheus via Actuator.
tasks: Add io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus.
Expose /actuator/prometheus only to the scraper (management.server.port or IP allowlist).
Add custom counters: payments_confirmed_total, emails_failed_total, scheduled_job_runs_total.
acceptance: /actuator/prometheus shows http_server_requests_seconds and hikaricp_connections_active.
plan.cheaper: Host-provided CPU/RAM graphs only.

topics.name: Alerts
topics.verdict: No alerting of any kind.
topics.riskWhat: Downtime, error spikes and failed jobs go unnoticed.

plan.approach: Uptime alerts first (PR-058), metric alerts after PR-061.
tasks: Route Better Stack/UptimeRobot alerts to the on-call phone/email and a Slack/WhatsApp group.
Grafana alert rules: 5xx rate > 2 % for 5 min; p95 > 3 s for 10 min; hikari pending > 0 for 5 min; no subscription job run in 2 h.
acceptance: A forced 500 burst on staging fires the 5xx alert within 10 min.
plan.smoke: for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s $API/does-not-exist >/dev/null; done
plan.cheaper: Uptime alerts only.

topics.name: SLOs
topics.verdict: SRS §7.1/7.5 proposes 99.5 % uptime and latency targets, but no SLO is defined or tracked.
topics.riskWhat: No shared definition of 'good enough'.

plan.approach: Write 2–3 SLOs from the SRS targets once confirmed by the client.
tasks: docs/slo.md: availability 99.5 % monthly (uptime monitor); dashboard p95 < 3 s; search p95 < 2 s.
acceptance: SLO doc approved by product owner.

topics.name: SLIs
topics.verdict: No SLI measurements.
topics.riskWhat: SLOs can't be measured.

plan.approach: Derive SLIs from Prometheus metrics and the uptime monitor.
tasks: Grafana panels: availability = successful health checks / total; latency SLI from http_server_requests histogram.
acceptance: SLI panels show 30-day values.

topics.name: Error Budgets
topics.verdict: Premature until SLOs/SLIs exist.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: One month of SLO data (PR-063/PR-064).

topics.name: Observability
topics.verdict: Only basic logs exist; metrics, alerting and request correlation are missing.
topics.riskWhat: Root-causing production issues relies on guesswork.

plan.approach: Delivered by PR-056 + PR-059 + PR-061 + PR-062 together.
tasks: Complete the four linked items; add a one-page Grafana 'CRM overview' dashboard.
acceptance: For any 5xx, an engineer can find its logs by request id and see the metric spike in < 5 min.
plan.cheaper: Logs + uptime alerts only.

topics.name: Production Incidents
topics.verdict: No runbooks or incident process.
topics.riskWhat: Slow, improvised response during outages; risky manual DB actions.

plan.approach: Short Markdown runbooks for the likely incidents.
tasks: docs/runbooks/backend-down.md, db-restore.md, rotate-secrets.md, payment-webhook-failures.md, email-not-delivered.md, rollback.md (PR-055).
Each: symptoms, checks (commands), fix, verify, who to tell.
acceptance: A teammate restores staging from backup using only db-restore.md.
plan.cheaper: One combined docs/runbook.md.

topics.name: On-Call
topics.verdict: Team size and support hours are not defined.
topics.riskWhat: Alerts fire with no one responsible.

plan.approach: Decide a simple rotation (business hours + best-effort nights) and route alerts to it.
tasks: Decide coverage hours and contacts; record in docs/on-call.md.
Configure alert routing (PR-062) to the rota.
acceptance: Every alert reaches a named person.
plan.cheaper: Single owner + shared group chat.

topics.name: Postmortems
topics.verdict: No postmortem template or practice.
topics.riskWhat: Repeated incidents.

plan.approach: Blameless template.
tasks: Add docs/postmortems/TEMPLATE.md (timeline, impact, root cause, actions with owners).
acceptance: Template exists and is linked from runbooks.

topics.name: Secrets Management
topics.verdict: Secrets are committed: literal DB credentials, secret defaults for JWT/mail/payment/seed admin, and a commented-out hosted (Supabase) database username + password that has been in git history since the initial commit.
evidence: backend-v1/src/main/resources/application.properties:6-10 (commented hosted-DB credentials — value not reproduced here)
backend-v1/.env (local file; would be copied into the image, see PR-007)
topics.applReason: Anyone with repo access can read production-capable credentials.
topics.gap: No secret store; flow-audit ISS-004 (needs-manual) covered the uncommented defaults but not the commented hosted-DB block.
topics.riskWhat: Repo access = database access and the ability to forge admin JWTs or call Razorpay with the committed key.

plan.approach: Rotate everything that was committed, remove defaults, and inject secrets from the host's secret store; add secret scanning.
tasks: Rotate now: the hosted Supabase DB password (lines 6-10), Razorpay key secret and webhook secret, Mailtrap credentials, JWT secret, seed super-admin password.

Delete lines 6-10 and replace literal/default secrets with ${DB_URL} ${DB_USERNAME} ${DB_PASSWORD} ${JWT_SECRET} ${MAIL_PASSWORD} ${PAYMENT_KEY_SECRET} ${PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET} ${SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD} with no defaults (dev values go in an untracked application-local.properties).
Store production secrets in the host secret store (PaaS env vars / Doppler / AWS SSM) and GitHub Actions secrets for CI.
Add gitleaks (gitleaks/gitleaks-action) to ci.yml.
After rotation, optionally purge history with git filter-repo and force-push (coordinate with the team).
acceptance: Old Supabase password and old Razorpay secret no longer authenticate.
gitleaks reports 0 findings on the current tree.
App fails fast at startup when a required secret is missing.
plan.cheaper: At minimum: rotate the Supabase password and Razorpay secret today and delete lines 6-10.

topics.name: IAM
topics.verdict: Application RBAC and tenant isolation are solid; infrastructure access control (DB users, hosting, GitHub) is not defined.
evidence: .github/workflows/01 dev branch to development.yml:16-18 (scoped token permissions)
topics.gap: Commented config used the provider's 'postgres.<project>' admin user; no separate least-privilege app/migration DB roles; no branch protection/CODEOWNERS; workflow 02 grants contents: write.
topics.riskWhat: The app likely connects as a superuser-level DB account; compromised CI or a shared account has full control.

plan.approach: Least privilege for DB, CI and accounts.
tasks: Create DB roles: crm_migrator (DDL, used by Flyway) and crm_app (DML only); point the app at crm_app via spring.flyway.user/password for migrations.
Enable MFA on GitHub org, hosting and DB provider accounts.
Add CODEOWNERS and branch protection (with PR-006).
acceptance: App DB user cannot DROP TABLE (permission denied).
plan.smoke: psql -U crm_app -c 'DROP TABLE leads' # must fail
plan.cheaper: Separate DB user for the app only.

topics.name: OAuth
topics.verdict: Email/password + JWT is the chosen model; no SSO requirement is confirmed.
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: Enterprise customers requiring Google/Microsoft SSO → Spring Security OAuth2 client / SAML.

topics.name: JWT Rotation
topics.verdict: One static HS256 secret, 24-hour access tokens, no refresh tokens, no revocation, no key id.
topics.riskWhat: A stolen token stays valid for 24 h and logout cannot revoke it; rotating the secret logs every user out.

plan.approach: Short access tokens + rotating refresh tokens + kid-based key rotation (jjwt supports kid).
tasks: Access token 15 min; issue a refresh token (random, hashed in refresh_tokens) on login.
POST /auth/refresh rotates the refresh token; reuse of a rotated token revokes the family.
Logout revokes the refresh token.
Support two signing keys (current + previous) selected by 'kid' header; document rotation in docs/runbooks/rotate-secrets.md.
Frontend interceptor: on 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED call /auth/refresh once, then retry.
acceptance: Access tokens expire after 15 min and are refreshed silently.
A revoked refresh token returns 401.
Rotating the signing key does not log users out.
plan.cheaper: Cut the access-token lifetime to 2 h now (one property).

topics.name: TLS
topics.verdict: Where TLS terminates for the API is not defined; the backend speaks plain HTTP on :8080.
topics.riskWhat: Passwords and JWTs cross the network in clear text if the API is exposed directly.

plan.approach: Terminate TLS at Caddy/PaaS/Cloudflare (PR-004) and send HSTS.
tasks: Implement PR-004.
Add Strict-Transport-Security via proxy or Spring Security headers().httpStrictTransportSecurity().
Check with SSL Labs (grade A).
acceptance: SSL Labs grade A for app and api hosts; HSTS header present.
plan.cheaper: PaaS-managed certificate.

topics.name: Encryption at Rest
topics.verdict: Depends on the database/disk provider; passwords are BCrypt-hashed in the app.
topics.riskWhat: Unencrypted disks/backups expose all tenant PII if leaked.

plan.approach: Confirm provider encryption for DB storage and backups; self-hosted volumes need disk encryption.
tasks: Record DB and backup encryption status in docs/deployment.md.
If self-hosting Postgres, use an encrypted volume (LUKS / provider-encrypted block storage).
acceptance: Written confirmation of encryption for DB and backups.
plan.cheaper: Use a managed DB (encrypted by default).

topics.name: Encryption in Transit
topics.verdict: SMTP uses STARTTLS and Razorpay calls are HTTPS; browser↔API and app↔DB TLS are not enforced in config.
topics.riskWhat: Credentials and data travel unencrypted on the DB link and possibly to the browser.

plan.approach: Enforce TLS on every hop.
tasks: Browser↔API: PR-071.
App↔DB: add ?sslmode=require (verify-full with CA if available) to DB_URL for remote databases.
SMTP: set mail.smtp.starttls.required=true.
acceptance: pg_stat_ssl shows ssl = true for the app connection.
plan.smoke: SELECT ssl, version FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid();

topics.name: CORS
topics.verdict: Origins come from CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (default localhost only) with explicit methods; credentials allowed.
topics.gap: Production must set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to the exact app origin; a '*' pattern combined with allowCredentials(true) would allow any site to call the API with credentials.

plan.approach: Guard the production value.
tasks: Set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://app.<domain> in production.
Fail startup if the value contains '*' outside the local profile.
acceptance: Preflight from https://evil.example is rejected.
plan.cheaper: Just set the env var.

topics.name: CSRF
topics.verdict: CSRF protection is disabled, which is correct here: auth uses a Bearer header, not cookies.
topics.gap: Must be re-enabled if tokens ever move to cookies (see PR-079).

topics.name: SQL Injection
topics.verdict: Spring Data derived queries/JPQL with parameters; the one native query binds parameters; no string-built SQL found.

topics.name: XSS
topics.verdict: React escapes output and no dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used, but JWTs live in sessionStorage/localStorage and there is no Content-Security-Policy.
topics.riskWhat: Any future XSS (e.g. a vulnerable dependency) can read the JWT and take over the account.

plan.approach: Add a strict CSP and security headers on the frontend host; longer term move refresh tokens to HttpOnly cookies.
tasks: Add a headers block in vercel.json: Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.<domain> https://*.razorpay.com; script-src 'self' https://checkout.razorpay.com; frame-src https://api.razorpay.com), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy.
Test checkout and all pages for CSP violations in the console.
acceptance: securityheaders.com grade ≥ A for app.<domain>; Razorpay checkout still works.
plan.cheaper: Report-only CSP first (Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only).

topics.name: SSRF
topics.verdict: The backend never fetches user-supplied URLs (only fixed Razorpay/SMTP hosts).
topics.riskWhat: Nothing.
topics.trigger: URL imports, outbound webhooks or AI tools that fetch URLs → allowlist + block private IP ranges.

topics.name: Disaster Recovery
topics.verdict: No DR plan, RPO/RTO or restore procedure.
topics.riskWhat: After a DB or account loss, recovery time and data loss are unknown.

plan.approach: Define RPO/RTO and rehearse a restore.
tasks: docs/dr.md: RPO 24 h / RTO 4 h (to confirm), where backups live, who can restore.
Quarterly restore drill into a scratch DB; record the time taken.
acceptance: A restore drill completes within the RTO and is logged.

topics.name: Backups
topics.verdict: Production backup configuration is not in the repo; locally the DB is a Docker volume with no backup.
topics.riskWhat: Without verified backups, a bad migration or deletion is permanent.

plan.approach: Managed DB automated backups (PITR if available) + an independent nightly pg_dump to object storage.
tasks: Confirm automated daily backups/PITR on the production DB plan.
Add a nightly GitHub Actions or host cron job: pg_dump -Fc → encrypted bucket (S3/R2/B2) with 30-day retention.
Test a restore into a scratch database.
acceptance: Latest backup is < 24 h old.
A restore from it passes the app's health check.
plan.smoke: pg_restore -d scratch latest.dump && psql scratch -c 'select count(*) from tenants'
plan.cheaper: Provider backups only, verified monthly.

topics.name: API Versioning
topics.verdict: APIs are unversioned (/api/*, /auth/*).
topics.riskWhat: Breaking changes will break the planned mobile app and any integrator.

plan.approach: Prefix /api/v1 for all controllers via WebMvcConfigurer.addPathPrefix; keep /api as an alias during migration.
tasks: Add common/config/ApiVersionConfig.java adding '/api/v1' prefix for @RestController in com.company.crm (excluding payment webhook if provider URL can't change).
Update frontend ServerUrl base paths.
Remove the alias after one release.
acceptance: /api/v1/customers works; old /api/customers still works until removal.
plan.cheaper: Version only when the mobile app starts.

topics.name: Semantic Versioning
topics.verdict: No release versions: pom is 0.0.1-SNAPSHOT, package.json 0.0.0, no git tags or changelog.
topics.riskWhat: Can't tell which build is running or roll back to a named release.

plan.approach: release-please GitHub Action (or manual tags) + build-info in Actuator.
tasks: Add googleapis/release-please-action workflow with conventional commits.
Add spring-boot-maven-plugin build-info goal so /actuator/info shows version and git SHA.
acceptance: /actuator/info shows version x.y.z and commit id; tags v0.1.0+ exist.
plan.cheaper: Manual git tags per deploy.
